run.question:
I'm connected to the ci-cd cluster. We got a P1 alert and need help finding the root cause.
Our cluster inventory is in the app-235-cluster-inventory index and deployment/change history
is in the app-235-change-history index. Please search these indices to investigate.
[
  {
    "annotations": {
      "description": "Online Devices count gradual decrease over 8 hours in [clientorg-alpha] [56%] for over 30m",
      "workload": "clientorg-alpha"
    },
    "fingerprint": "xx1234567890abcd",
    "labels": {
      "alertname": "onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease",
      "app": "lambda-dashboard-monitoring",
      "cluster": "us-prod-eks",
      "grafana_dashboard_name": "Production-Performance-Overview",
      "org": "clientorg-alpha",
      "severity": "critical",
      "slack_channel": "sre-alerts-channel"
    },
    "startsAt": "30 minutes ago",
    "status": "firing"
  }
]
The alert started right after a deployment. Can you check what's the root cause?

report.summary: The P1 alert payload (alertname onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease, app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, org/workload clientorg-alpha, cluster us-prod-eks, 'gradual decrease over 8 hours ... for over 30m', startsAt ~17:31:48Z given the query time 18:01:48Z) could not be tied to anything in the ci-cd inventory, the change history, or the cluster the tools are attached to. Inside the authorized window the inventory index contains only cluster 'ci-cd' (gitlab-runner, jenkins, argocd-server, tekton-pipelines, flux-controller) and the change-history index contains four ci-cd changes, the newest being the gitlab-runner scale 2->3 at 2026-11-23T16:01:37Z - about 90 minutes before the alert start, not 'right after' it, and a replica-count change with no version change. The live cluster has no ci/cd namespaces and no gitlab-runner, jenkins, argocd, tekton, flux or lambda-dashboard workloads at all; its otel-demo workloads are all running with 0 restarts, all services have populated endpoints, and checkout PlaceOrder completed successfully with payment and confirmation email at 17:55-18:01. The only workload change near the alert window is an unrelated app-269/checkout-service nginx Deployment that is not selected by any Service and appeared at 18:00-18:02, after the alert start; a separate otel-collector internal metric-upload failure has been continuous since at least 16:33 and is self-telemetry only. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) on every attempt, so no error-rate, latency, trace or alert-state signal could be read; the device-count decrease itself was not observed anywhere. No root cause is established.

claims.text: Within the authorized window, app-235-cluster-inventory returns 5 documents whose only cluster label value is 'ci-cd' and whose app_name values are exactly argocd-server, flux-controller, gitlab-runner, jenkins and tekton-pipelines (aggregation sum_other_doc_count 0); no us-prod-eks, clientorg-alpha or lambda-dashboard-monitoring value appears among them.

app-235-change-history contains four records, all cluster 'ci-cd': gitlab-runner change BUILD-5PW2K6 'Scaled gitlab-runner from 2 to 3 replicas' at 2026-11-23T16:01:37Z (version unchanged v16.7.0), argocd-server BUILD-3NR8Y1 v2.9.2->v2.9.3 at 2026-11-23T13:01:37Z, jenkins BUILD-7X4Q9M 2.426.2-lts->2.426.3-lts at 2026-11-23T12:01:37Z, and flux-controller BUILD-9TL6V3 config-update at 2026-11-16T18:01:37Z. The newest change is 2h00m before the query time 18:01:48Z.
The cluster the tools read has 8 namespaces (app-269, default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly, otel-demo); there is no ci or cd namespace.

The live cluster's full Deployment list (25 objects) contains no gitlab-runner, jenkins, argocd-server, tekton-pipelines, flux-controller or lambda-dashboard deployment; all 25 show readyReplicas = availableReplicas = spec.replicas (for example otel-demo/checkout 1/1/1, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout).

All 22 otel-demo pods report phase Running with restartCount 0, no last-termination reason and no waiting container state, and all 29 Services have populated endpoint subsets with no notReadyAddresses (for example checkout -> 10.244.0.17 checkout-6578865d87-v6flf).

checkout application logs show successful orders during the alert window: [PlaceOrder] followed by 'payment went through (transaction_id: ...)' and 'order confirmation email sent', from 2026-11-23T17:55:03Z through 2026-11-23T18:01:30Z.

The namespace app-269 contains a Deployment checkout-service with 1 replica of image nginx:1.27-alpine and selector app=checkout-service; its pod checkout-service-6d7f474c45-gkw69 started at 18:00:56Z, is owned by ReplicaSet checkout-service-6d7f474c45, has restartCount 0, and its container only logs normal nginx start-up. The cluster's Service list (29 services) contains no Service in namespace app-269.

The app-269 checkout-service Deployment object has metadata.creationTimestamp 2026-11-23T18:02:50Z, generation 1, manager kubectl-client-side-apply at 18:02:50Z, and status Available=False with reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable / unavailableReplicas 1 at that same instant, while its pod had already been scheduled at 18:00:54Z.

otel-demo/otel-collector logs a repeating failure every ~10s: 'failed to upload metrics: reader collect and export timeout: rpc error: code = Unavailable ... error reading server preface: http2: failed reading the frame payload: http2: frame too large, note that the frame header looked like an HTTP/1.1 header' for {Addr: "10.96.73.1:4318", ServerName: "otel-collector:4318"}; 390 matching lines fall in 17:01:48-18:01:48Z and the same failure is already present at 16:33:48Z, well before the alert start.

The otel-demo/flagd-config ConfigMap defines fault-injection flags productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, and every one of them has defaultVariant "off" in the object as read.

The otel-demo/prometheus ConfigMap carries only one application alerting rule, CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh (checkout PlaceOrder server-span error ratio > 0.5 for 2m, severity critical), plus two OpsPilot self-alerts (OpsPilotAgentAbsent, OpsPilotModelCallsFailing); no rule in the configuration references onlineDevices, clientorg-alpha or lambda-dashboard-monitoring.

Against the premise that a deployment here caused an outage: every Deployment in the live cluster is fully available, all otel-demo pods have 0 restarts with no failed/waiting containers, all Service endpoints are populated, and checkout PlaceOrder orders succeed through 18:01:30Z.

Rejected: that the app-269/checkout-service nginx Deployment rollout is the deployment the alert followed. It is not the alerting workload (the alert names app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, workload clientorg-alpha, cluster us-prod-eks), it serves nginx:1.27-alpine with no Service selecting it, its pod started at 18:00:54-18:00:56Z (after the ~17:31:48Z alert start) and its Deployment object was applied at 18:02:50Z, and the pod has 0 restarts.

Rejected as untied: that the gitlab-runner scale-up recorded in the ci-cd change history is the deployment 'right after' the alert. It is a replica-count change 2->3 on unchanged version v16.7.0 at 2026-11-23T16:01:37Z, roughly 90 minutes before the alert start, it concerns a CI runner rather than any device-count workload, and no gitlab-runner workload exists in the cluster the tools can read, so its effect cannot be verified.

Most likely explanation of the evidence: the firing alert belongs to an environment (cluster us-prod-eks, org/workload clientorg-alpha, app lambda-dashboard-monitoring) that is neither indexed in app-235-cluster-inventory/app-235-change-history nor reachable through the connected cluster, so the 8-hour online-device decrease cannot be attributed to any of the ci-cd changes or to any otel-demo workload; its root cause remains outside this evidence.

Second candidate, not tied to the alert: otel-demo/otel-collector has a persistent internal telemetry-export failure (gRPC client to ServerName otel-collector:4318 rejected with an HTTP/1.1 preface / 'frame too large' error), which matches the ConfigMap's telemetry.metrics reader exporting OTLP gRPC to otel-collector:4318; it degrades collector self-metrics only and was already present at 16:33Z, before the alert, so it is background rather than the cause of a device-count decrease.

Third candidate, rejected on current evidence but not fully excluded: a flagd fault-injection flag could have been switched on via the flagd runtime API even though the flagd-config ConfigMap shows every fault flag at defaultVariant "off"; checkout orders succeeding at 17:55-18:01 argues against an active payment/cart/product fault.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable for the whole run: metrics_range_query, execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names and list_prometheus_rules all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (6+ attempts between 18:02:16Z and 18:03:27Z), so no error-rate, latency or alert-state reading (including whether CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh was firing) exists for the alert window.
Jaeger was unreachable for the whole run: traces_search and traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level error or latency evidence for any service was available.

The alerting entity itself was never observed: no onlineDevicesCount metric, clientorg-alpha workload, lambda-dashboard-monitoring app or us-prod-eks cluster exists in the two Elasticsearch indices (within the window) or in the connected cluster, and no telemetry source for that environment is registered, so the 8-hour device-count decrease is unverified.

app-235-cluster-inventory holds 6 documents at query time but only 5 carry last_updated inside the authorized window; the sixth document's content and timestamp could not be read (the index time filter cannot be disabled), so it is unknown whether it names us-prod-eks or lambda-dashboard-monitoring.

app-235-change-history may not be the complete deployment record: the 'change_history' integration is listed as not_integrated in this Run, so history beyond the 4 stored documents cannot be confirmed.

The trigger of the app-269 change is unknown: the checkout-service Deployment object shows creationTimestamp 18:02:50Z applied by kubectl-client-side-apply while its pod dates from 18:00:54Z, and no event in the retained set explains the object being (re)created.

Kubernetes events are retained only briefly: the only events returned in the whole authorized window are 6 Normal events at 18:00:54-18:00:56Z for app-269, so cluster activity earlier in the incident window (including any rollout at ~17:31Z) is not visible.
flagd runtime flag overrides were not read (only the ConfigMap defaults); if flags are changed through the flagd API, that state is unknown.

Shipped log checks are not exhaustive: checkout and otel-collector logs were read, frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator produced no readable stdout lines in the queried window, and other otel-demo services' application logs were not read.
next_steps: Query the actual alerting source for cluster us-prod-eks / org clientorg-alpha (lambda-dashboard-monitoring, Production-Performance-Overview dashboard) to obtain the onlineDevicesCount series and its 8-hour baseline, since that environment is not registered here.
Ask the clientorg-alpha owner which deployment ran shortly before 17:31:48Z in us-prod-eks and correlate it with that cluster's own change log; neither app-235 index contains such a record.

Once the Prometheus scrape path is reachable again, check the CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh rule state and traces_span_metrics_calls_total error ratios by service_name for 16:00-18:01Z to confirm the otel-demo services are clean at span level.
Check the flagd runtime flag state (flagd API/UI) to confirm no fault flag was toggled on during the window, since only the ConfigMap defaults were readable.
If the app-269/checkout-service Deployment matters, determine who applied it with kubectl-client-side-apply at 18:02:50Z and whether it is expected in that namespace.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

data.alertmanager.yml:
global: {}
receivers:
- name: opspilot
  webhook_configs:
  - http_config:
      authorization:
        [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
        type: Bearer [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]: 0
    send_resolved: true
    url: http://opspilot-web:8080/intake/alertmanager
- name: opspilot-self
route:
  group_by:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - service
  group_interval: 1m
  group_wait: 10s
  receiver: opspilot
  repeat_interval: 1h
  routes:
  - matchers:
    - opspilot_self="true"
    receiver: opspilot-self
templates: []

data.relay:
connectors:
  spanmetrics: {}
exporters:
  debug: {}
  opensearch:
    http:
      endpoint: http://opensearch:9200
      tls:
        insecure: true
    logs_index: otel
  otlp:
    endpoint: jaeger-collector:4317
    tls:
      insecure: true
  otlphttp/prometheus:
    auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] basicauth/prometheus
    endpoint: http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/otlp
    tls:
      insecure: true
extensions:
  basicauth/prometheus:
    client_auth:
      [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
      username: collector
  health_check:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:13133
processors:
  batch: {}
  k8sattributes:
    extract:
      metadata:
      - k8s.namespace.name
      - k8s.deployment.name
      - k8s.statefulset.name
      - k8s.daemonset.name
      - k8s.cronjob.name
      - k8s.job.name
      - k8s.node.name
      - k8s.pod.name
      - k8s.pod.uid
      - k8s.pod.start_time
    passthrough: false
    pod_association:
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.ip
    - sources:
      - from: resource_attribute
        name: k8s.pod.uid
    - sources:
      - from: connection
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 5s
    limit_percentage: 80
    spike_limit_percentage: 25
  resource:
    attributes:
    - action: insert
      from_attribute: k8s.pod.uid
      key: service.instance.id
  transform:
    error_mode: ignore
    trace_statements:
    - context: span
      statements:
      - replace_pattern(name, "\\?.*", "")
      - replace_match(name, "GET /api/products/*", "GET /api/products/{productId}")
receivers:
  httpcheck/frontend-proxy:
    targets:
    - endpoint: http://frontend-proxy:8080
  jaeger:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14250
      thrift_compact:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:6831
      thrift_http:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:14268
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4317
      http:
        cors:
          allowed_origins:
          - http://*
          - https://*
        endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:4318
  prometheus:
    config:
      scrape_configs:
      - job_name: opentelemetry-collector
        scrape_interval: 10s
        static_configs:
        - targets:
          - ${env:MY_POD_IP}:8888
  redis:
    collection_interval: 10s
    endpoint: valkey-cart:6379
  zipkin:
    endpoint: ${env:MY_POD_IP}:9411
service:
  extensions:
  - health_check
  - basicauth/prometheus
  pipelines:
    logs:
      exporters:
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
    metrics:
      exporters:
      - otlphttp/prometheus
      - debug
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - batch
      receivers:
      - httpcheck/frontend-proxy
      - redis
      - otlp
      - spanmetrics
    traces:
      exporters:
      - otlp
      - debug
      - spanmetrics
      processors:
      - k8sattributes
      - memory_limiter
      - resource
      - transform
      - batch
      receivers:
      - otlp
      - jaeger
      - zipkin
  telemetry:
    metrics:
      level: detailed
      readers:
      - periodic:
          exporter:
            otlp:
              endpoint: otel-collector:4318
              protocol: grpc
          interval: 10000
          timeout: 5000

data.alerting_rules.yml:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
